  • propels the person back up. Some energy is lost as heat and sound. (6 marks)

questions.question: What are stable equilibrium and unstable equilibrium positions?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans. A body is in stable equilibrium if, when slightly displaced, it experiences a
  • restoring force or torque that brings it back to its original position. In potential energy
  • curve it is the minimum energy position.
  • Example: A ball resting at the bottom of a bowl. If nudged, it rolls back to the bottom.
  • A body is in unstable equilibrium if, when slightly displaced, it experiences a force or
  • torque that moves it further away from its original position. In potential energy curve
  • it is the maximum energy position.
  • Example: A ball balanced at the top of a hill. If nudged, it rolls down and never returns
  • to the top.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Define projectile motion. What are the assumptions made in the study of projectile motion?
questions.solution_html:
• motion?

  • determined entirely by the effects of gravitational acceleration and air resistance. To
  • analyse the motion of a projectile, we represent the projectile as a particle with an
  • acceleration (due to gravity) that is constant in both magnitude and direction. We’ll

  • velocity- i.e. projectile motion is two-dimensional. Projectile motion can be analysed
  • as a combination of horizontal motion with constant velocity and vertical motion with
  • constant acceleration.

questions.question: What are stable equilibrium and unstable equilibrium positions?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans. A body is in stable equilibrium if, when slightly displaced, it experiences a
  • restoring force or torque that brings it back to its original position. In potential energy
  • curve it is the minimum energy position.
  • Example: A ball resting at the bottom of a bowl. If nudged, it rolls back to the bottom.
  • A body is in unstable equilibrium if, when slightly displaced, it experiences a force or
  • torque that moves it further away from its original position. In potential energy curve
  • it is the maximum energy position.
  • Example: A ball balanced at the top of a hill. If nudged, it rolls down and never returns
  • to the top.
